articles.summary: Monster Hunter Wilds at IGN: walkthroughs, items, maps, video tips, and strategies
articles.body:
Monster Hunter Wilds is the first of the "sixth generation" of the Monster Hunter series. IGN's Monster Hunter Wilds guide is a thorough guide with a detailed walkthrough, helpful tips, thoughtful how-to guides, and lists of all encyclopedic topics like weapons, armor, monsters, and more.

See a Monster Hunter Wilds Monsters List - this includes links to detailed guides with tips, weaknesses, and material drops for every monster.

Just starting out? Need some guidance? Check these guides out!

Armor is a huge part of Monster Hunter and not only dictates your defense and resistances, but your skills and appearance, too!

All Low Rank Armor in Monster Hunter Wilds

See Armor for an overview of how it works. This should answer all of your questions!

Monster Hunter Wilds Walkthrough and List of Chapters

Our MH Wilds walkthrough includes details on how to prep for the challenges to come, so you know you won't leave camp unprepared!

articles.title: Priority: Tuchanka - Mass Effect 3 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about the Priority: Tuchanka Mission, including how to get through all combat encounters, where to find
articles.body:
This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about the Priority: Tuchanka Mission, including how to get through all combat encounters, where to find all collectibles, and pick the right dialogue choices for your playthrough.

The conclusion of this mission leads directly to " Priority: Citadel 2 ". When this happens, a number of optional quests and interactions will be closed: you will not be able to start and / or complete them, and you will lose out on any credits, XP, War Assets, and Reputation associated with them.

So before starting this Mission, MAKE SURE to complete the following quests and activities:

There's also a number of interactions you can have with various characters that will also be missable:

Docks: Holding Area - Garrus and 2 interactions with Kelly Chambers (3 if you told her to change her identity).

Huerta Memorial Hospital - Dr. Michel and Thane Krios.

Presidium Commons - Joker, EDI, Matriarch Aethyta, Liara, the two businessmen arguing about VIs.

Finally, there are three Citadel Side Missions that you cannot complete until AFTER "Priority: Tuchanka"! Thus you needn't worry about having these hanging around in your Journal:

War Assets: (note that the Krogan and Salarian War Assets are normally mutually exclusive) Turian: Turian 43rd Marine Division (90 TMS) Turian Engineering Corps (110 TMS) Turian Seventh Fleet (90 TMS) Krogan: Clan Urdnot (300 TMS) Krogan Clans (300 TMS) Urnot Wrex / Wreav (30 / 25 TMS) Salarian: Dr. Mordin Solus (25 TMS, if he survived Mass Effect 2) Salarian First Fleet (150 TMS)

Turian: Turian 43rd Marine Division (90 TMS) Turian Engineering Corps (110 TMS) Turian Seventh Fleet (90 TMS)

Krogan: Clan Urdnot (300 TMS) Krogan Clans (300 TMS) Urnot Wrex / Wreav (30 / 25 TMS)

Salarian: Dr. Mordin Solus (25 TMS, if he survived Mass Effect 2) Salarian First Fleet (150 TMS)

Dr. Mordin Solus (25 TMS, if he survived Mass Effect 2)

After completing one of the two initial Tuchanka Side Missions (either " Attican Traverse: Krogan Team " or " Tuchanka: Turian Platoon "), your STG doctor will say that the cure itself is ready, but needs a method of dispersal across the Krogan. Here you can say...

"You've infected them before" for +2 Renegade Points .

As he goes through the list of options, your doctor will realize that they can use The Shroud, which was originally part of a massive array built by the Salarians to clean Tuchanka's atmosphere, then later used to disperse the original Genophage virus. At this, you can say...

"That was devious" for +2 Paragon Points .

"That was clever" for +2 Renegade Points .

Prerequisite: Complete either " Tuchanka: Turian Platoon " or " Attican Traverse: Krogan Team "

Location: Krogan DMZ - Aralakh - Tuchanka

Go to the Krogan DMZ and then to Tuchanka in the Aralakh system. In orbit around Tuchanka, choose the Shroud Facility to begin this mission. As noted above, you'll need to have completed either " Attican Traverse: Krogan Team " or " Tuchanka: Turian Platoon " first, so that your STG Doctor can complete the cure and begin figuring out how to disperse it.

While you're here, you may want to consider getting the following Search and Rescue items from the Krogan DMZ's other systems (although Nith is admittedly optional since it only contains Fuel):

When you select the Mission on Tuchanka itself however, you've got a problem: a Reaper Destroyer has showed up and is using the Shroud to poison Tuchanka's atmosphere instead. There's no way a ground team can distract it long enough for the team to slip in, so Shepard asks Victus for Turian support.

Convince Victus for his support by saying either... "But this is for Palaven" for +2 Paragon Points . "Keep your word" for +2 Renegade Points .

"But this is for Palaven" for +2 Paragon Points .

"Keep your word" for +2 Renegade Points .

Once the plan has been formulated, you can say... "Everyone up for this?" for +2 Paragon Points . "Failure isn't an option" for +2 Renegade Points .

"Everyone up for this?" for +2 Paragon Points .

"Failure isn't an option" for +2 Renegade Points .

As everyone leaves however, you get an urgent call in the Vid Comm Room from the Salarian Dalatrass, who lets you know that the Shroud was tampered with years ago to prevent any cure from being effective. Plainly she doesn't believe the Krogan will be co-operative after you cure the Genophage: at this, you can say...

"Yes, this could work" for +2 Paragon Points .

"No, krogan aren't peaceful" for +2 Renegade Points .

Either way, she offers you significant Salarian support in exchange for ensuring the cure won't work.

Squad Tactics: You'll be facing a lot of armored enemies, so Garrus and James make good choices.

You'll be facing a lot of armored enemies, so Garrus and James make good choices.

Unique Dialogue: For the most unique dialogue, pick Liara and Garrus . If Garrus isn't available, pick EDI . Liara and Javik is another good pair.

For the most unique dialogue, pick Liara and Garrus .

Shepard's Loadout: Bring a Shotgun for the initial Husk fight. The Scorpion Heavy Pistol can be very useful in taking out the Brutes and Ravagers .

Bring a Shotgun for the initial Husk fight.

The Scorpion Heavy Pistol can be very useful in taking out the Brutes and Ravagers .

As you head towards the Hollows, Shepard is oddly quiet, and Eve will ask if there's something on your mind. Here you can pick either...

"[Reveal Shroud sabotage]" for +2 Paragon Points .

"[Say nothing for now.]" for +2 Renegade Points .

Unfortunately even if you decide to reveal the sabotage, Shepard has no time to actually spit it out, as you get attacked on the way: the Hollows have been overrun.

As soon as you touch down you will face an onslaught of Husks. The best way to handle them is to strafe around the area with a Shotgun, but the arena is open enough for maneuvers around the Husks. Use your Squad powers when you get trapped, but otherwise the shotgun should be all you need.

When the Husks are all dead, you'll get into a lengthy cutscene with dialogue choices. From the outset, pick "What clan are you?" on the left to make sure you can get as many Morality Points as possible here. The exact names of the options will vary depending on who the Krogan Leader is:

"The salarian is with me" OR "He's saving your people", "Count me in", "The krogan have earned it OR "Leave it in the past" ( +6 Paragon Points total).

"Fall in line", "Everyone had better help", "Expansion could be a problem" OR "I'd want revenge, too" ( +6 Renegade Points total).

After this you'll then be in a Tomkah on the way to the Shroud. Yet again Eve will notice Shepard and ask if they want to say something. This decision will affect the tone of this Mission's climactic scene:

Pick "[Reveal Shroud sabotage]" to allow your STG doctor to adjust the cure for +15 Paragon Points . If you destroyed Maelon's data in Mass Effect 2, then Wrex will take this honesty as an apology, which he accepts.

If you destroyed Maelon's data in Mass Effect 2, then Wrex will take this honesty as an apology, which he accepts.

Pick "[Say nothing for now]" to withhold the sabotage from your STG doctor for +2 Renegade Points .

Suddenly the Tomkah convoy stops, and you hop out to investigate. Before you do that however, you should sweep the area for a bevy of loot:

Med Kit - Immediately to your left from your starting position, in the middle of the clearing.

Graal Spike Thrower - This Shotgun is leaning up against the railing at the edge of the area, directly in front of you after picking up the Med Kit above.

Shotgun Smart Choke - Turn around and head back to your starting position, then head left (or counter-clockwise) along the Tomkah wheels. The first item is this mod, by the kneeling Krogan working on the Tomkah.

Pistol Magazine Upgrade - Found further to the left, between the wheels of another Tomkah.

Once you've picked everything up, talk to the Krogan Scout, and things will escalate where Shepard is forced to order Eve be moved immediately. This strands Shepard behind on the highway, and you'll have to figure out an alternate route. Follow the Mission Maker to the doorway across the gap and head into the ancient catacombs.

You'll now find yourself in the dark catacombs. This area is pitch black and a bit of a maze, but luckily Shepard has a torch and you have us. You may be bewildered by the many twists and turns, but in reality the various paths lead to the same place. There are some collectibles down here, which we'll direct you to, starting with dropping down the end of the first, large staircase.

Ancient Krogan Artifact #1 - 8,500 Credits. After dropping off the end of the first large staircase at the beginning of the catacombs, turn left on the spot to see a doorway. Head through here and drop down the ledge, then head directly forward through another doorway into a room with a column in the middle. On the right-hand wall will be this as a wall painting.

Ancient Krogan Artifact #2 - 8,500 Credits. Backtrack to the previous room and turn left to find another doorway on the left-hand wall, which has you drop into small trench in the ground: here Eve will talk about Kalros, the mother of all Thresher Maws. Head left from here and you'll find this painting of Kalros directly ahead.

Ancient Krogan Artifact #3 - 8,500 Credits. From Artifact #2, continue through this area in an effective U-Turn, and the only way forwards will be a doorway on your left into a hallway. Check the right-hand wall of this hallway for the third and final wall painting, depicting Krogan riding war beasts.

Soon you will find a Ravager corpse at the bottom of the stairs leading out. This scene will have alternate dialogue if you haven't yet completed " Attican Traverse: Krogan Team ". Continue up the stairs and you'll eventually make your way up to the surface again.

As you continue forwards a few meteoric barrages will drop Ravagers and Cannibals. The Ravagers have tough Shields and fire highly damaging shots like rocket launchers. If you are hit by their missiles your own shield will evaporate fast. Stay far away and behind cover to deal with them. You can pretty much ignore the Cannibals and focus on the Ravagers for now. If you stick Ravagers with Viper shots or use Armor Piercing Rounds they go down easy.

Jump across the gap in the bridge ahead. In the next area you encounter a Brute, but you can handle it much better if you keep your distance. Hang far back on the bridge and snipe the Cannibals. Inch forward until the Brute appears and, while it's still ambling out of the doorway ahead, pummel it with everything you've got. Hopefully it won't get a chance to go on the offensive, but if it does remember that you can tap the Sprint button to dodge roll out of the way.

You will eventually come to a large area with a doorway flanked by large Krogan statues. Between these pour several Cannibals and a pair of Ravagers. Run to the small, raised area and take cover behind the low wall facing the Ravagers and fire at them. The Cannibals should ignore you, but the Husks won't! Take out the Cannibals quickly so you can run around and hit the Husks with your Shotgun.

Now cross the bridge. A View Prompt will help you see the Krogan Leader's Tomkah being chased by Kalros and take out a tiny chunk of the bridge. Kalros destroying the bridge shouldn't stop you: you can cross a narrow gap on the right-hand side and leap over it.

Begin crossing the large plaza with the Krogan statues and then you'll come up against more Cannibals and Husks. This time a trio of Marauders join them from the far side. Just be sure to have your Shotgun ready for the Husk onslaught while you work the Marauders Shields down. Once you're ready, look for collectibles in the area.

SMG Scope - Before leaving the area with the first Marauders of the level, search the left-hand side of the arena for this Weapon Mod. It'll be near the stairs connecting it to the second area.

Assault Rifle Extended Barrel - As you leave the arena with the Marauders you climb down and then up two sets of stairs. Head left and up some more stairs to find this Weapon Mod in the corner.

When you drop down the gap on the right-hand side of the stairs you'll initiate a cutscene that moves you to the next area.

The next cutscene will detail the plan to get the Reaper Destroyer out of the way: by using a pair of Maw Hammers to summon Kalros and keep the Destroyer occupied. Here you have two pairs of options for Morality Points:

"What about the risks?" and "Be safe" ( +2 Paragon Points total).

"We've done crazier things" and "Let's get it done ( +2 Renegade Points total).

Additionally, if Wrex is the Krogan Leader and you either spared Maelon's data in Mass Effect 2 or are back on good terms with Wrex after destroying it, you'll get an exclusive Paragon Interrupt that you can pull for +5 Paragon Points .

After the cutscene concludes, take cover and fight off more Cannibals. You shouldn't find these guys too surprising to deal with by now. Once they're all dead, head for the stairs on the left-hand side of the area.

M-5 Phalanx - Climb the stairs after killing the Cannibals, then turn left to find this pistol.

After getting the pistol, head to the far end and leap over the gap. The Reaper above has noticed you, but luckily the Turian ships return to the fight to keep it distracted for you. Sprint as fast as you can across the rubble to the Maw Hammers, and the last fight of the level.

The goal here is to activate two spots, one up some stairs on the right and one just across from it on the left. Each hammer has a Reaper leg guarding it that can crush you, but that's the least of your worries: Brutes will spawn infinitely to hamper your progress (but luckily they only spawn in two at a time, not counting the two that are initially there).

That said, this section ends once you activate the Maw Hammers, so if you're fast and clever, you can actually just Sprint straight to one, activate the Maw Hammer, then rush across to the opposite side of the battlefield and hit the second one. This tactic is much easier if you are an Infiltrator with Tactical Cloak , since you can slip past the Brutes undetected. You still need to pause to avoid the Reaper legs guarding each Hammer either way, however.

Hit both of the Maw Hammers, and Kalros will show up and destroy the Reaper, however the Shroud takes a big blow in the ensuing fight. With the Destroyer destroyed, Shepard heads into the Shroud to see how their STG Doctor is doing.

After the Hammers are activated you will be privy to an important dialogue scene. There are many different outcomes that are made possible thanks to the choices you've made in all the games in the Trilogy before this point.

The first outcome point occurs when Shepard first enters the room, concerning the fate of Eve. It occurs via exposition from the STG Doctor when Shepard first enters the room:

If you saved Maelon's research data in Mass Effect 2, then Eve will have lived through the procedure.

If you destroyed Maelon's research data in Mass Effect 2, then Eve will have died while you were fighting the Reaper. Starting Mass Effect 3 without importing a Mass Effect 2 Profile will always give this result, even if you used the Genesis 2 DLC comic.

What happens next depends on whether you decided to reveal the Shroud's sabotage to your STG Doctor, Eve and the Krogan leader back in the Tomkah convoy:

If you warned Eve and the Krogan Leader about the Shroud Sabotage back in the Tomkah convoy, then when Shepard arrives your STG Doctor will have countered it already. Their ascent up the elevator is automatic, meaning they'll always sacrifice their life to cure the Genophage.

If Mordin is your STG Doctor, you can pull a Paragon Interrupt as he heads into the elevator. While it doesn't dissuade him from his task, it allows you to part ways by saying either...

You'll also get +15 Reputation for curing the Genophage.

If you DIDN'T reveal the Shroud sabotage to Eve and the Krogan Leader back in the Tomkah convoy, then your STG Doctor will notice something is wrong, opening up the possibility to stop them from dispersing the Genophage cure. Here are your options:

Pick "[Explain sabotage]" to justify your reasons for +2 Paragon Points , letting you choose either... "I was wrong" for +2 Paragon Points . "I need the salarians" for +2 Renegade Points .

"I need the salarians" for +2 Renegade Points .

Pick "[Delay him]" to try and obstruct the STG Doctor for +2 Renegade Points .

If you picked either "[Delay him]" or "I need the salarians" as described above, you'll now have several options to choose from:

Pick "I'm not stopping you" / "I was wrong. Go ahead" to let the STG Doctor ascend in the elevator, sacrificing their life to cure the Genophage for +15 Reputation .

Pick "I'll stop you if I have to" to try and stop your STG Doctor with a Renegade Interrupt: Pulling the Renegade Interrupt shoots your STG Doctor dead for +15 Renegade Points . Ignoring the Renegade Interrupt lets them go up the elevator, sacrificing their life to cure the Genophage, getting you +15 Reputation .

Pulling the Renegade Interrupt shoots your STG Doctor dead for +15 Renegade Points .

Ignoring the Renegade Interrupt lets them go up the elevator, sacrificing their life to cure the Genophage, getting you +15 Reputation .

If Wrex is dead and Eve died while your STG Doctor synthesized the Genophage cure, you also have two Persuasion options to choose from: Pick the "Now isn't the time" Charm to convince the STG Doctor to walk away with their life for +15 Paragon Points . Pick the "Why?" Intimidate to convince the STG Doctor to walk away with their life for +15 Renegade Points .

Pick the "Now isn't the time" Charm to convince the STG Doctor to walk away with their life for +15 Paragon Points .

Pick the "Why?" Intimidate to convince the STG Doctor to walk away with their life for +15 Renegade Points .

Once you've made your choices, you'll then see the Shroud disperse the particles shortly before collapsing, and then you'll reconvene with the Krogan Leader in the Hollows. If Eve died, this scene will her funeral.

There are a wide variety of potential options here given the outcome of the Shroud finale, but rest assured that the upper-right option will give +2 Paragon Points , and the lower-right option will give +2 Renegade Points .

You'll then reconvene with Admiral Hackett over your decisions, and at last seal the deal with Primarch Victus for Turian support when the time comes to retake Earth. Garrus will then insist Shepard get some rest, despite their objections. You'll now be in another dream sequence where you chase after the boy, this time with inky black figures in the park and the voices of the dead echoing through the air. Shepard will then wake up and have a small chat with Liara over the fallen, then head to the Vid Comm room.

This time it's a conversation with the Salarian Councillor. You'll again have several potential options here, but as in The Hollows, the upper-right one will always give +2 Paragon Points , and the bottom-right one +2 Renegade Points . Either way you'll pick up a new Mission: " Priority: The Citadel 2 ".

Now you can explore the Normandy again to hear everyone's responses to the aftermath of Tuchanka.

CIC - Talk to Hackett on the Vid Comm, Traynor to get " N7: Cerberus Fighter Base ", and Joker / Garrus on the Bridge for +2 Reputation . If you saved Zhu's Hope on Feros in Mass Effect 1, you'll have an email that, once read, will give you the Zhu's Hope Colonists War Asset, worth 30 TMS.

If you saved Zhu's Hope on Feros in Mass Effect 1, you'll have an email that, once read, will give you the Zhu's Hope Colonists War Asset, worth 30 TMS.

Crew Deck - Talk to Liara, as well as EDI in the AI Core.

Engineering - Talk to Javik for +2 Reputation , and Engineer Adams to complete " Citadel: GX12 Thermal Pipe ". If Gabby and Ken are both present, you'll get Optimized Eezo Capacitors worth 15 TMS! You can also talk to Diana Allers for an interview. This will give +5 Reputation , and you can add +5 TMS to either the Krogan Clans (Charm) or Turian Seventh Fleet (Intimidate).

You can also talk to Diana Allers for an interview. This will give +5 Reputation , and you can add +5 TMS to either the Krogan Clans (Charm) or Turian Seventh Fleet (Intimidate).

You may notice in the Requisitions Terminal that the M-25 Hornet is now for sale from Batarian State Arms. We advise against buying it at this time, because you can pick it up for free in an upcoming Mission.
