articles.summary: Sony’s first “pro” controller for the PS5, the DualSense Edge, features removable back buttons, interchangeable analog sticks, unique profiles, and much more. Its intuitive user interface makes customization not only approachable, but encouraged, for everyone who can afford its premium price.
articles.body:
Sony’s first official foray into the “pro” controller scene has finally arrived with the DualSense Edge, a $200 answer to Microsoft’s $180 Xbox Elite Series 2 . Its design immediately feels familiar, but it comes standard with all the trappings you’d expect of a pro controller at this price: interchangeable back buttons, adjustable analog sticks, added grips, and customizable profiles. However, what makes it stand out is the deep integration of hardware and software at the system level that third-party controller makers simply can’t match, and the ingenuity of the new Function buttons make customizing and swapping between profiles second nature.

The DualSense Edge’s design doesn’t deviate much from that of the standard DualSense controller, making the transition from one to another a seamless upgrade with a minimal learning curve. That being said, it’s packed with plenty of exciting tech and makes high-end controller features more accessible to the wider PlayStation audience.

PlayStation DualSense Edge Wireless Controller

Everything comes neatly packed in a two-toned hardshell case that matches the white-and-black PS5 and is made from what appears to be the same plastic as the controller itself. Inside you’ll find the DualSense Edge front and center, as well as a small selection of accessories and interchangeable bits. There are two different back buttons – a half dome-shaped option and lever-style option – as well as two different convex analog stick heights to replace the default sticks with. Additionally, there’s a 9.1-foot-long, braided USB-C cable, as well as a small plastic mechanism that can be added to the top of the DualSense Edge to ensure the cable doesn’t accidentally get pulled out during gameplay. There’s even a small flap on the back of the case that allows you to charge the controller while it’s inside.

The most notable physical change between the DualSense Edge and standard DualSense is the addition of a Function button below each analog stick, allowing you to save or swap between custom profiles as well as adjust audio settings on the fly. This is paired with a slick interface on the PS5 that makes swapping between your profiles a breeze. You can even “pin” your four most commonly used profiles to the face buttons for quick access.

In addition to the Function buttons, the back of the DualSense Edge also sports some fancy pro-level features. Both analog triggers feature stop sliders to reduce the travel distance, with three presets available. You can choose between the full range, a medium-level range, and a short-range for more instantaneous activations. Additionally, you can adjust individual dead zones for each analog trigger in the software settings – but more on that later.

Below the stop sliders are the LB and RB slots where you can insert the optional back buttons. You can choose between lever-style or half-dome back buttons, both of which are constructed with a premium metal build. The levers are longer and shallower, following the curvature of the controller, and will be familiar to people who have used other pro-style controllers like the Xbox Elite. These lever-style buttons are a bit easier to press as they sit naturally against the controller grips.

The half-dome alternatives, on the other hand, are unlike any back buttons I’ve used before. They have a unique shape that’s similar to an analog stick cut in half and sit diagonally across the rear of the controller. They require more intentionality to press, but feel much sturdier than the lever-style options and less likely to see any accidental presses. The placement of the half-domes requires your middle fingers to rest much higher on the back of the controller, but also means they can easily be ignored when holding it normally. This makes them the less obtrusive back button option if you intend to keep them attached permanently. Otherwise, you can always remove them and store them in the case when not in use.

The DualSense Edge's killer feature is fully replaceable analog stick modules. While stick drift hasn't plagued the DualSense quite as much as Nintendo Switch Joy-Con, it still does occur, and it’s massively frustrating having to replace an entire controller when the problem surfaces under your thumbs. The DualSense Edge sidesteps this problem by letting you entirely swap out either stick module (replacements are sold separately for $20 apiece, far cheaper than I’d expected) if and when the sticks start to fail. I do wish Sony had simply outfitted the DualSense Edge with more reliable Hall effect sensors , which shouldn't be prone to drift in the first place, but including easily replaceable modules is a consumer-friendly option that I’m pleased to see nonetheless.

The analog sticks themselves are identical to those found on the standard DualSense controller, shape and all. As previously mentioned, there are also two interchangeable analog stick options: a tall, convex shape for more precise movements; and a short, convex shape meant for quicker, run-and-gun style play. Both sticks are made from a semi-hard rubber material with a textured surface for added grip. For what it’s worth, the short convex sticks are nearly identical to the PS1 to PS3-era PlayStation controllers, and feel great.

Some minor differences include textured rubberized grips on the inside of the controller stems and added texture to the ends of the L2 and R2 buttons to keep your fingers in place during gameplay. Both textures feature teeny tiny versions of the four iconic PlayStation symbols – a design choice that’s used even more heavily across the entirety of the controller than the standard DualSense.

In addition to these new pro-level upgrades, all of the standard DualSense features are here, including haptic feedback, adaptive triggers, built-in microphone, and more. To further distinguish itself from the default controller, the DualSense Edge has a slightly edgier (sorry) look with black face buttons, a black D-pad, and an all-black touchpad adorned with the iconic PlayStation symbols. This touchpad feels a bit more robust and has more of a squared-off edge. These changes are subtle enough that the DualSense Edge does work with the existing DualSense charging station, so no need to buy a new one.

For better or for worse, the overall ergonomics of the DualSense Edge haven’t evolved much, so those that find the standard DualSense uncomfortable to hold for long periods of time aren’t going to see much of a difference here. That said, it’s quite a bit heftier, weighing in at approximately 325 grams compared to the original DualSense at around 280 grams – or about a 16% increase in weight. It’s definitely noticeable upon first pickup, especially in the controller’s stems and throughout the center. However, it’s still lighter than the Xbox Elite Series 2, which weighs 345g before any modifications.

After connecting your DualSense Edge to your PS5 for the first time, you’ll have the option to run through a short tour that introduces you to its core features. This tutorial does a great job of introducing the Function menu and helps you create and customize your first profile.

Within each profile, there are a number of individual options you can customize. The first area lets you remap every single button on the DualSense Edge, as well as apply button assignments to the back buttons. It’s worth noting that this doesn’t update anything in the game you’re playing, so if a button prompt is displayed on screen, you’ll need to remember where you mapped it. The second section lets you adjust analog stick dead zones as well as choose from preset sensitivity curves. The final section allows you to adjust dead zones for the analog triggers. There are also options to adjust vibration and adaptive trigger intensity.

DualSense Edge – Settings and User Interface

Holding down the Function button brings up a small on-screen overlay menu that shows your four assigned profiles – one for each face button – as well as the option to create a new profile or adjust headphone volume and audio mix. When swapping to a different profile, the controller emits a small burst of haptic feedback and a notification lets you know the active profile has changed. It’s quick and fairly non-intrusive to your gameplay, but can be further customized or turned off completely, if you desire.

Creating, editing, and swapping profiles is extremely intuitive and the slick interface makes for an engaging experience throughout. The Custom Profiles section in the Settings app (which you can quickly jump to via the Function button) lets you view your four assigned profiles, and hovering over each one displays which buttons and settings have been adjusted at a glance, in case your naming convention wasn’t descriptive enough. There’s no limit to the number of unassigned profiles, so you’re free to experiment with all sorts of custom assignments before calling your favorites up to the majors in your shortcut slots. The PS5’s interface isn’t perfect, and at times can be downright baffling, but I think Sony nailed it with the approachability and simplicity of the DualSense Edge experience.

One area that didn’t see any substantial improvement over the standard DualSense is the life of the built-in rechargeable battery, which is something that’s been a common complaint of PlayStation’s controllers for years. During my testing, I received a low battery notification after about 4.5 hours of gameplay, and the controller lost power just shy of 5.5 hours. This number can and will likely vary, as it largely depends on the type of game you’re playing and which features the controller is using frequently – most notably, the more often the haptics fire, the shorter the battery life. Sony hasn’t given any official figures regarding expected battery life for the DualSense Edge, but it’s safe to say it’s definitely not significantly longer than the standard DualSense controller.

Maybe it’s that new controller feeling, but the default analog sticks and D-pad feel incredibly snappy compared to my existing DualSense controllers. Either way, it’s clear that the DualSense Edge is built well. Nothing feels cheap, but I can say that about the standard DualSense as well.

I spent a fair bit of testing time in Call of Duty’s Warzone 2.0 and DMZ modes, flexing my competitive chops a bit and putting the back buttons to good use. I mapped jumping and sliding to the back buttons for increased mobility, and tweaked the sensitivity options for the analog sticks to allow for quicker reactions. I also used the analog trigger stops on the back of the controller to ensure my gunfire was almost instant, but I was still able to switch back to the full range of motion for driving with a quick flip of the switch. While I can safely report none of these features instantly made me a noticeably better player, I will say that I felt more confident in my engagements specifically because my thumbs didn’t have to leave the sticks for even a split second.

One issue that I ran into, though, was that the built-in microphone on the controller picked up a lot of external audio – mainly button presses and quick stick flicks – and players on proximity chat were having difficulty hearing me. That said, most people will likely have headphones on, which would remedy that issue, but it’s worth noting that there don’t appear to be any substantial noise-canceling features on the DualSense Edge’s built-in mic.

The added flexibility of back buttons doesn’t just have to be for fast-paced first-person shooters or competitive play, though. You can customize them for added accessibility, or simply for personal preference. This differs from the system-wide accessibility settings that permanently remap buttons as you can essentially create game-specific loadouts. Don’t like the button used to pull up the character menu in a JRPG? Remap it. Having trouble with a difficult combo input in a fighting game? Remap it. For combat-heavy games like Elden Ring, you could map your dodge and block to the back buttons to ensure you never have to take your thumbs off the movement and camera controls during a difficult fight. There are tons of possibilities, and the ease in which you can program individual profiles and swap between them on the fly makes this a great controller option for just about anyone.

Another feature I appreciated was the ability to quickly create a new profile from within a game via the Function menu. This allows you to remap buttons, tweak analog stick or trigger sensitivity, and customize the back buttons, all without having to open a different app. After finalizing your new profile, you can quickly hop back to your game to test out your configurations in real time. If something doesn’t feel the way you wanted, you can easily jump back to the profile editor and tweak it with the push of a button. It makes the entire process of creating, editing, and testing custom profiles a seamless and natural experience.

I did notice that the analog sticks make a very subtle and tactile popping sensation when moving away from the center location. It’s something that I completely forgot about once I started playing a game, but it’s worth noting, even if it’s more of a minor nitpick. On the flipside, I was pleasantly surprised that the half-dome back buttons make a satisfying click when pressed in reverse, and made for a nice fidget toy during cutscenes.

You'll find only a few Sha-Chi Amber Fragments in the Mountain of Imprisonment in Phantom Blade Zero . This is an optional location that you can enter from Meigu Lake, and only after you have completed the Illusory Pipa side quest. Keep reading this guide to find the locations of the four Sha-Chi Amber Shards in Mountain of Imprisonment.

All Mountain of Imprisonment Sha-Chi Amber Shards

There are four Sha-Chi Amber Fragments in Mountain of Imprisonment. Check the map above for their general location and the rest of the guide for the individual spots.

Mountain of Imprisonment Sha-Chi Amber Fragment 1

From the Commander’s Platform , where you fought Commander Bi, go north and start climbing the mountain. You’ll see a passage with red shrines : go through it.

Keep going up until you find a small area with enemies. Before the path that you need to follow, you’ll see a tower with an archer . Climb the tower's ladder, defeat the archer, and open the purple chest.

Mountain of Imprisonment Sha-Chi Amber Fragment 2

This is dropped by Kui Yanyan, The Deranged — the boss that you’ll fight after the Shrine Outer Gate.

Mountain of Imprisonment Sha-Chi Amber Fragment 3

In the Shrine Outer Gate , you might have noticed two locked doors — one in front of the bell, the other to the left. The shard is past the left door; to open it, you'll need to activate the lift in the lower area, Cavern Passage, where you can find Liu Yi , the NPC from the Hero's Lament side tale.

To activate the lift, you need the Missing Lift Crank , which is dropped by Kui Yanyan, The Deranged . Once you have it, insert the crank, use the lift, and interact with the corpse in the small room — it has the shard.

articles.title: GTA 6 Shatters Streaming Records Before It Even Launches Globally
articles.summary: GTA 6 is already breaking records, despite not having even been out for a full day yet.
articles.body:
GTA 6 is already breaking records, despite not having even been out for a full day yet.

According to StreamCharts, GTA 6 shattered livestreaming viewership records following its release in New Zealand. Streamers began grinding the game at the earliest hours of the morning here in the United States thanks to handy loopholes on Xbox, allowing them to get a head start on things. As of 12:30 UTC today, the game crossed 6.38 million concurrent viewers across Twitch, YouTube, and Kick. This is nearly four times the previous record holder, which was Valorant's closed beta.

Twitch also provided first details about the game's performance using its own internal data to IGN.

GTA 6 smashed the Valorant on Twitch record, which stood at 1.7 million concurrent viewers in 2020.

On Twitch, GTA 6 is at tens of millions of hours watched, just a couple hours in. The equivalent of more than 1,500 years of nonstop viewing.

The equivalent of more than 1,500 years of nonstop viewing.

Top GTA Streamer Rubius reached 311k live viewers for GTAVI within an hour of starting his broadcast.

GTA 6 in North America is technically not available to play yet but the streamer has already seen: Twitch viewership is up 111% compared with this time last week. At one point early this morning Twitch had more than 3.3 million live viewers in the GTA 6 category.

Twitch viewership is up 111% compared with this time last week.

At one point early this morning Twitch had more than 3.3 million live viewers in the GTA 6 category.

Twitch recently revealed to IGN that GTA 5 has accumulated 9 billion hours watched over the course of its entire lifetime, making it an absolute juggernaut for the platform. It's one of the most-watched games and it's likely that GTA 6 will retain get at least one or two more big boosts in viewership. The game is rumored to come to PC early next year and its online mode is also expected sometime in 2027, both of which will likely be events in their own rights.

IGN recently spoke with a number of content creators about how they're planning to handle GTA 6 and how long they think this game will remain relevant. Although some streamers believe this game will only be lucrative for a couple of weeks, others think there's potential for it to be mined for months and years to come.

IGN gave the game a 10/10 , noting that the game is simply unmatched in its depth, quality, and detail. The game is currently the highest-rated game in history on Metacritic with an unprecedented 99 average score.

"Exquisitely detailed, endlessly ripe for experimentation, and uncompromisingly engineered, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played," reads an excerpt from our review.

For more GTA 6, check out our breakdown of how long the game can be depending on how you play, how it performs on Xbox Series S , and much, much more.

articles.title: The Wachowskis Move to Reclaim The Matrix Rights From Skydance
articles.summary: The future of The Matrix franchise is suddenly in doubt, as Lilly and Lana Wachowski move to reclaim the copyright to the iconic sci-fi franchise from Warner Bros.
articles.body:
The future of The Matrix franchise is looking increasingly murky. According to The Puck Report , Lana and Lilly Wachowski have formally notified Warner Bros. of their move to reclaim the copyright to the iconic sci-fi franchise.

If successful, the Wachowskis would regain the rights to the series on the 30th anniversary of the original film's release in 2029. This move comes as the studio is developing a fifth The Matrix movie , with Drew Goddard attached to write and direct and Lana Wachowski herself executive producing. That project may give the Wachowskis extra leverage in their negotiations with Warners.

The Matrix Movies in (Chronological) Order

Will this derail development on The Matrix 5? Not necessarily. The site also notes that WB's new parent company Skydance seems confident in its ability to negotiate a new deal, building on previous successes renegotiating the copyright for The Godfather and acquiring The Terminator rights in 2011. The Puck Report also alludes to a potential legal hurdle on the Wachowskis' side, as it could be argued that the original The Matrix screenplay was part of a work-for-hire arrangement with Warner Bros. back in the '90s.

All of this may suggest that the more likely outcome is that the Wachowskis negotiate a new, more lucrative deal and Skydance retains the rights to The Matrix for the foreseeable future. Despite Lilly Wachowski publicly distancing herself from the property , The Puck Report writes, "From what I hear, the sisters have been encouraging of the newest sequel and have even increased their involvement lately."

Little is currently known about The Matrix 5 beyond Goddard's involvement. There's currently no release date, nor is it clear whether series stars Keanu Reeves and Carrie-Anne Moss will return or if the focus will shift to a new cast of cyberpunk martial artists. But the studio seems to have high hopes for the sequel, despite its predecessor, 2021's The Matrix Resurrections, proving to be a box office dud. It certainly didn't help that the film debuted during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic and premiered on HBO Max the same day as it did in theaters, prompting a lawsuit from Village Roadshow .

articles.title: Burger King’s Chocolate Whopper Prank Is Being Turned Into a Real Burger
articles.body:
In 2018, Burger King posted a Chocolate Whopper as an April Fool’s Joke. Nearly a decade later, the decadent burger is actually coming to life.

The Chocolate Whopper is coming to Burger King Korea’s new flagship restaurant, the Flameground, which recently launched its first location in Seoul. Flameground somehow turns Burger King food into a luxurious dining experience, showcasing the fast-food chain’s most experimental creations.

Burger King Korea accounts have shared AI-generated renderings of the Chocolate Whopper’s concept: layers of sauces and brownie patties encased in a chocolate fudge bun. We'll have to wait until the burger launches on November 19 to see what it actually looks and tastes like.

Unfortunately, the Chocolate Whopper is getting an extremely limited rollout. The burger isn’t even coming to general Burger King Korea locations, and is instead entirely restricted to the single Flameground restaurant, which requires a reservation.

The generated rendering is jam-packed, to say the least. Each burger is handmade, and orders are restricted to one per person with daily quantity limits. The Chocolate Whopper will also only be available as a dine-in experience, no take-out allowed, so Burger King is really trying to stop you from sharing.

Ahead of the launch, Burger King also reshared the original April Fool's prank video. The original prank featured some candied tomatoes the real version understandably skips out on.

Burger King Korea launched its first Flameground restaurant this past September. The Seongsu location currently offers three signature burgers: the K-Cube Galbi, the Philly Cheese Steak, and the Memphis BBQ. These are priced between ₩12,900 and ₩13,900, equivalent to around $10 USD. The restaurant has yet to announce pricing for the Chocolate Whopper.

The entire Burger King franchise has taken to wacky marketing, though most of the chain’s big promotions stick to licensed collaborations. For example, Burger King Italy just launched a Magic: The Gathering meal with an exclusive deck box everyone has been trying to get their hands on. Surprisingly, the fast-food chain has yet to announce any new food items inspired by GTA 6 , which features the parody restaurant Burger Shot.

articles.title: A GTA 6 Location Was Teased by Rockstar All the Way Back in 2021 — And What's Inside Was Worth the Wait
articles.summary: In 2021, Rockstar fans believed that a GTA 6 screenshot was snuck into the GTA trilogy collection, but there's more to this theory than meets the eye.
articles.body:
SPOILER WARNING: This article features details on a GTA 6 Easter egg. Although it won't ruin the game's story or anything like that, we recognize some people want to organically discover and find interesting things on their own. You've been warned!

In 2021, Rockstar Games released the somewhat controversial remastered collection of the PS2 era GTA titles. It was... a mess, to say the least. However, one notable thing came from that collection, but fans weren't sure if it actually meant anything. There was a picture of a house in this new version of GTA: San Andreas that wasn't there in the original game, and it didn't look like a location from any other GTA game. Fans theorized this was actually our first look at GTA 6 ... and it turns out, they were right!

The house is real. It's located in Leonard County, in the suburb of Belville (shoutout Jared from the GTA mapping community for discovering this). However, that's just the tip of the iceberg. If you approach the house's garage, you can actually break in. Upon entry, it becomes clear this is a lair for some kind of conspiracy theorist. These aren't just ordinary in-universe ramblings — they're from someone who believes they are in a video game.

All credit goes to Jared from the GTA VI Mapping server. The house is located in Belville. ( — GTA Wiki (@GTAWikiOfficial) November 18, 2026

All credit goes to Jared from the GTA VI Mapping server. The house is located in Belville. (

Various notes and writings on the wall point out that they can't leave Lenoida at all. They tried to purchase a ticket to Los Santos and couldn't, nor could they drive out of the state, and instead are planning to get a boat to try and escape. They also noted that there are an extraordinary amount of doppelgangers in reference to NPCs, that there is nothing behind closed doors, their own neighbors can't enter their homes, and that people phase through walls or "glitch." There's also a graph that shows a comically large spike in violent crime and a bunch of 6s written all over the place, likely poking fun at some of the people who drove themselves mad theorizing about this very game.

Perhaps one of the most notable bits is that this conspiracy theorist has determined two people, who go by "J" (Jason) and "L" (Lucia), are immune to whatever problems they are experiencing, suggesting they have freedom and autonomy. Ironically, they may have the least amount of autonomy, though, since they are controlled by the player, but they respawn, are largely free of longterm legal consequences, and can cause tons of mayhem, so they're less restricted than NPCs.

It's a very silly Easter egg, and one that leans into the absurdity of the GTA community in many ways. It's unclear whether this house was always meant to be like this, or if someone at the studio decided to have some fun with it after they saw how mad it drove fans. Either way, it gave me a good chuckle.

In related news, GTA 6 is already shattering all kinds of records despite not being out globally. The game is driving tons of traffic to Twitch, YouTube, and Kick, with millions of people just watching the game. As for its critical reception, GTA 6 got a 10/10 from IGN and its critical praise has been echoed across the industry. In addition to being nominated for Game of the Year , GTA 6 is currently tied with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time as the highest rated game of all-time on Metacritic . While its position could change as more reviews trickle in over the next few weeks, it's clear this game is a gargantuan hit (though that likely isn't surprising).

articles.title: 43 Army Members Reenlisted in Exchange for Paid Time Off to Play GTA 6
articles.summary: If you’ve been following the GTA 6 hype train, you’ll probably remember the time that an army battalion went viral for offering service members four days of paid time off to play Rockstar's highly-anticipated game if they reenlisted.
articles.body:
If you’ve been following the GTA 6 hype train, you’ll probably remember the time that an army battalion went viral for offering service members four days of paid time off to play Rockstar's highly-anticipated game if they reenlisted.

The news became a hot topic after a flyer advertising the paid leave was first shared online back in August. Now that GTA 6 is almost upon us (or, in some regions, already out ), we’ve finally gotten an update on how many soldiers actually took up the battalion's offer.

The flyer, dated July 28, concerned the 9th Engineer Battalion in Fort Stewart, Georgia, and promised a “special reenlistment incentive” by giving eligible service members four days off to play the game from November 20 - 23, 2026. This was done specifically to “coincide with the highly anticipated release of the video game Grand Theft Auto VI,” with the goal of “promoting retention, boosting morale, and rewarding the continued dedication of the Soldiers within the 9th Brigade Engineer Battalion.”

Three months later, military-focused news outlet Task and Purpose has shared a follow-up on this incentive, confirming that 43 members of the battalion took up the offer. Two of these soldiers spoke with the platform — one being combat engineer Sgt. Jamire Smith, who says he signed up for the GTA 6-specific PTO and an additional six more years in the armed forces. However, this extra time came with a nice $60,000 bonus, owed to his special training learning how to drive heavy breaching vehicles.

“I’m all campaign. I’m all about the heist. I think I have a good 24 hours to waste on it,” he told the outlet. “I was actually in the process of getting out, I was towards my final stages of getting out … but my company and the battalion helped me navigate through that and they showed me that there’s still a need for me, and that I am still a clear and value asset to the team, and so that’s really what drove me to say ‘let’s keep going, let’s keep driving.’ Maybe be a lifer in this, since I already made it my career.”

Task and Purpose even got in touch with the person responsible for coming up with the campaign, Staff Sgt. Brittany Wolfer, a career counselor who explained why she chose to use the game as an eye-catching way to get soldiers to stay in the service.

“I brought it to my battalion commander and he’s a little bit older, but he did play GTA 2 at some point, so he was like, ‘Yeah I’m down for it,’” Wolfer explained. “I came into [the unit], there hadn’t been a counselor for about eight months, so there [were] a lot of gaps and things that were falling through, because the soldiers didn’t have that presence within the formation. This was just a way to grab people’s attention and kind of be like, ‘Hey, here I am. I’m the person you’re gonna come talk to,’ and [it] kind of snowballed from there.”

Wolfer made it clear that she knows the GTA 6-focused PTO dates won’t be a “deciding factor” in someone’s decision to reenlist, but said the idea was a way to “bridge that gap” between soldiers and their senior command “to where that lower soldier still knows that their battalion commander or their senior leadership cares about them and sees what they’re interested in. And that’s kind of what this was for.”

GTA 6 releases for players in the United States at 12am ET / 9pm PT. Despite not even being officially out yet, it has already scored eight nominations at the 2026 Game Awards , and is one of the highest-rated games in Metacritic history . You can check out our review for the game right here on IGN, which we scored a glowing 10 out of 10.

articles.title: GTA 6 rouba as paradas: como o jogo virou vitrine de hits musicais | G1
articles.standfirst: De Travis Scott a Keith Richards, músicas de GTA VI acumulam milhões de reproduções e dão continuidade à força da franquia em transformar o game em vitrine para músicas.
articles.summary: De Travis Scott a Keith Richards, músicas de GTA VI acumulam milhões de reproduções e dão continuidade à força da franquia em transformar o game em vitrine para músicas.
articles.body:
Travis Scott (à esquerda), Fuerza Regida (ao centro) e Keith Richards (à direita) fazem parte do álbum do GTA 6. — Foto: Reprodução

Mesmo antes de qualquer fã jogar o primeiro minuto de GTA 6 , muita gente já sabia músicas da trilha de cor. Até o jogo chegar, à 0h desta quinta-feira (19), as faixas do álbum oficial já somavam milhões de reproduções no Spotify, e o Brasil era o segundo país que mais dava play na playlist do game, atrás só dos Estados Unidos.

O disco, " Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album ", feito em parceria com a gravadora Atlantic Records, tem 34 músicas originais, com nomes como Travis Scott, Tame Impala e Yung Lean. Na série, a música vai além da trilha sonora: ela ajuda a construir o universo de cada jogo.

A fórmula já tinha funcionado em GTA V , de 2013, que ganhou um álbum com músicas feitas para o jogo por artistas como A$AP Rocky e Tyler, the Creator. Uma das faixas, "R - Cali", de A$AP Rocky, passa hoje de 171 milhões de plays no Spotify.

Com GTA VI , o efeito veio antes mesmo do lançamento: “Suzuki”, do grupo Fuerza Regida, já soma quase 70 milhões de reproduções, e “RHYNO”, de Travis Scott, mais de 20 milhões. Até Keith Richards, aos 82 anos, entrou na onda: as visitas à página do guitarrista dos Rolling Stones no Spotify cresceram 1.200% no dia em que as primeiras músicas saíram.

Segundo dados divulgados pelo Spotify após o lançamento das seis primeiras músicas, em setembro, as faixas somaram 4,1 milhões de reproduções na plataforma nas primeiras 24 horas.

No dia do lançamento, além de Keith Richards, as páginas dos artistas registraram aumento nas visualizações na plataforma:

GTA 6. — Foto: Divulgação/Rockstar Games

Músicas inéditas de GTA VI acumulam milhões de reproduções

A primeira leva de músicas foi disponibilizada em 17 de setembro, quando a Rockstar, produtora do jogo, anunciou oficialmente o álbum. Outras faixas foram lançadas nas semanas seguintes. Entre as mais ouvidas até agora estão:

"Suzuki", de Fuerza Regida : 69,6 milhões de reproduções;

"Flower In A Hurricane", de Justice, King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard, SZA e Tame Impala : 45,8 milhões de reproduções;

"Last Thing You Need", de Morgan Wallen : 44 milhões;

"Sexy Magic", de CA7RIEL & Paco Amoroso, PinkPantheress, Fred again e Etienne de Crécy : 20,3 milhões;

"Macacoa 2000", de Rauw Alejandro : 19 milhões.

GTA V também transformou músicas criadas para o jogo em sucessos

O álbum de GTA V, “The Music of Grand Theft Auto V, Vol. 1: Original Music”, tinha 18 faixas de artistas de diferentes gêneros, como A$AP Rocky, Tyler, the Creator, Wavves, Neon Indian e The Chain Gang of 1974.

Algumas das músicas mais ouvidas do álbum no Spotify são:

"r - Cali", de A$AP Rocky : mais de 171 milhões de reproduções;

"Sleepwalking", de The Chain Gang of 1974 : cerca de 80 milhões;

"The Set Up", de Favored Nations : aproximadamente 57,6 milhões;

"Welcome to Los Santos", de Oh No : cerca de 48,5 milhões;

"Hold Up", de Marion Band$ : aproximadamente 47,5 milhões.

No total, o álbum já acumula mais de 611 milhões de reproduções no Spotify, segundo levantamento do ChartMasters, site especializado em monitorar dados da indústria musical.

Uma das histórias mais curiosas envolve "Nowhere to Go", da cantora Nite Jewel. A faixa foi criada exclusivamente para GTA V e se tornou a música mais conhecida da artista no Spotify, com mais de 8 milhões de reproduções.

De Michael Jackson a Dr. Dre: a música sempre fez parte da identidade de GTA

Antes de investir em álbuns com músicas originais, a franquia já havia conquistado espaço pela seleção de canções famosas que apareciam nas rádios dos jogos.

Em GTA Vice City , lançado em 2002 e ambientado em uma cidade inspirada em Miami nos anos 1980, os jogadores podiam ouvir sucessos como:

A trilha sonora chegou a ganhar sete álbuns lançados em parceria com a Sony Music, reunindo músicas das diferentes estações de rádio do game.

Dois anos depois, GTA San Andreas levou os jogadores para uma Califórnia fictícia dos anos 1990. A seleção musical acompanhava o cenário, com destaque para o hip-hop e o rap da Costa Oeste americana.

Já em GTA V, a Rockstar ampliou a variedade musical, com mais de 240 músicas licenciadas em suas rádios, além das faixas originais produzidas para o jogo.

articles.body:
The official Grand Theft Auto VI Chapter 2 walkthrough includes strategies for main missions, suggestions for side activities, where directions for optional missions, and plenty more. In GTA 6’s Chapter 2 – Paradise Lost, Lucia has to figure out what’s next for her and Jason as they lay low near the small town, Port Gellhorn.

Click on a link below to jump to that specific section of this guide:

GTA 6 Chapter 2 Main Mission Walkthroughs

You’ll play through 18 main missions in GTA 6’s Chapter 2. Below are complete guides for each, including initial mission objective descriptions and rewards. Please be careful when scrolling as some mission titles, thumbnails, and descriptions contain spoilers or allude to spoilers .

• Tap to Reveal • Tap to Reveal • Tap to Reveal • Tap to Reveal

After a few introductory missions, Kelly County is at your will. You can go beyond it any time you’d like, but for the purposes of this guide, we’re focusing on the immediate area you’ll explore in Chapter 2.

Keep an eye out for WAiNK scan spots that on flyers and posters put up around Leonida. They might lead to an optional mission or something else! If you find yourself at a tourist destination, hotel lobby, or waiting area with information pamphlets or maps, take a look at them. Sometimes they hint at side objectives or can add new locations to your map. Books and magazines throughout the world can do the same, so it’s worth taking a moment to flip through them.

Mud and other messes can also appear on Jason and Lucia. You can clean it off by having them take a shower or by selecting "Freshen up" at any sink.

You’ll find the folks of Port Gellhorn can be more difficult to intimidate than most of the tourists of Key Lento. Some may be armed. Be careful!

Moses can only register cars using money from your BuckMe account. Similarly, you can only use RydeMe with BuckMe payments. The kinds of payment a shop or service accepts is shown by the illuminated payment method on the top right of the screen. Some locations accept either. If you need either cash or money added to your BuckMe account, visit an ATM to make a withdraw or deposit.

Kelly County is home to far more than Port Gellhorn. If you feel up to it, take a drive around the country roads to encounter all sorts of activities.

Don’t forget to scan vehicles the the WAiNK it app to log them in your Vehicles collection. You can see all the cars, aircrafts, and other vehicles you’ve spotted so far in the Progress menu.

In addition to being home to lots of farmland, Kelly County also has gorgeous hills and forests. You can study new kinds of critters here.

Starlet Motel is a dump with limited amenities but there are just enough to be helpful. If you go out front to the disgusting pool, you’ll spot weights and kettlebells around. Use these to work on Lucia’s strength and boost her health bar.

As you complete missions, it’s good to walk around and see if there’s anyone new to meet. They often won’t award you anything special, but isn’t friendship its own reward? Right? No? Well, if an interesting conversation isn’t enough for you, sometimes you’ll spot someone who needs help around the motel, and they may reward you if you solve their problem.

Three cats live around the Starlet Motel. Petting them and feeding them not only rewards you with a Focus boost and points toward a professional Criminal Profile, but you’ll also gain a small progress boost toward the next Focus level depending on how much time you spend with a cat.

To pet a friendly animal, focus on them with L2 / LT , then praise them. Some won’t want to be pet, but often if you keep praising them, they’ll approach you, allowing for more interaction options.

The best way to make money in Chapter 2 is to steal cars and sell them to Moses. Some go for enough to make the money Brian paid Jason for jobs look like chump change.

If you've just hit a gang operation or took a mission that involves messing with one, grab a random car rather than taking your own . There's a good chance the gang will send people to go after you when you're out and about, and it can be expensive to get your car fixed if its engine gets damaged if you're attacked while driving.

If you press both thumbsticks while in enemy territory, you'll not only see the movements of foes, but also potentially see hidden valuables, health items, and weapons highlighted within a short distance. Keep an eye out especially for items in gold – these represent Key Valuables. The valuable you spot will then be tracked on the map, which can be helpful for return hits if you fail to collect it the first time you spot it. You can also get help finding all key valuables with the individual illegal operation guides.

When taking part in some grand theft auto, make sure no one is too close when you steal a car. It's best to try to take cars that are alone in the back of parking lots, away from any busy roads. If someone spots you stealing a car from the road, they'll call the cops.

The more you explore Leonida, the more likely you’ll unlock optional missions. Below are a selection of missions you can start and finish in Chapter 2. Keep in mind that these missions can be found earlier than Chapter 2 and well after you’re done with Chapter 2. To see the full list of Optional Missions and how to start them, visit our complete guide .

Like optional missions, you’re not limited by the chapter you’re in to investigate most illegal operations and activities. Anything that takes place in Key Lento is off limits, though, as Jason and Lucia are Wanted in the area throughout Chapter 2. Below are a selection of illegal operations and side activities near the Chapter 2 safe house.

To see all illegal operations you can hit in Leonida, visit the comprehensive illegal operations guide .

articles.title: Wanted Guide - How to Escape the Cops and Clear Heat - GTA 6 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Wanted levels return in Grand Theft Auto VI in the form of escalating star rankings, but with greater nuance than past GTA games thanks to the new Heat system.
articles.body:
Wanted levels return in Grand Theft Auto VI in the form of escalating star rankings, but with greater nuance than past GTA games thanks to the new Heat system.

Use the below headings to jump to a specific section of this guide page.

Keep in mind that wanted levels aren't necessarily tied to what you do, but to what's been reported, and there's a few different ways that can happen:

You commit a crime in front of a police officer.

A witness calls the police to report the crime (you can often see and hear them do this).

Someone calls in a crime they think you committed, even if you didn't (wrong place, wrong time).

The crime is at a large-enough scale that a dispatcher immediately sends police out to your location (explosions, trespassing in high security areas, stealing a plane, etc.).

I put maybe five or six guys in this trailer park to sleep (and kicked a dog, I’m so sorry), and never even got a star. Where you are and who sees you are important factors to raising Wanted levels!

Because your wanted level in GTA 6 is based on what's reported , and not just committing the crime, the police response time can vary wildly. You can even commit multiple crimes without facing consequences for a long period if no one reports it, or you can leave the area before the police respond. This is why it's important to understand the different types of stars you can earn, and how the Heat system works.

While knowing the star ratings and heat indicator icons are important, you also need to listen to the police chatter you can hear over the scanner. The scanner is unlocked during an early story mission in Chapter 1. You can listen to the police dispatch review what’s being reported, what direction they believe you’re heading in, and even offer insight to understanding brief windows during which you can lose pursuing cops.

Before we get into the different Star (or Wanted) levels, we need to go over how the Heat System works. If earning a Wanted level means turning the oven on, Heat is the time it takes to cool down even after you turn it off. In other words, upon escaping the cops after earning a few Stars, the residual heat in the area will make it easier for you to be pursued by the police again. If you're in an area and the stars are red, it means you have Heat, and being spotted by the police or committing another crime will fill those red stars back in with white, and the chase will resume. The unfilled stars with the red outline mean the cops don't know what you look like, but committing another crime in the area can have the same effect of filling in all your previous stars.

This area is also marked by a red outline and faint red shading on your map.

We’ll go over this again in the section about Wanted (Star) levels, but clearing Heat icons is also important for avoiding detection between the time your crime has been reported (Gray Stars) and when the police spot you (White Stars).

Thankfully, GTA 6 gives you Heat icons that tell you exactly how the cops are tracking you. You need to clear these as quickly as you can.

Appearance – The cops know your appearance. If the crime is premeditated, make sure you put on a mask first to avoid gaining this icon. If you get the appearance heat, changing accessories or your hairstyle can clear it.

Vehicle – If you're still driving the vehicle the cops saw you in, you need to ditch it for a new car, or get it repainted.

Outfit – You need to change your clothes. It's always a good idea to keep a spare outfit in your trunk for this purpose. Just make sure to change clothes and/or store your gun before you ditch your car. You can also buy new clothes or steal a temporary set of clothes from any shop that sells them after threatening the store clerk.

Visible Weapon – iIf you're holding a pistol or sidearm, press L1 / LB to put it away. Longarms need to be stashed in your trunk or dropped altogether since you can't hide them.

Partner – You and your partner were spotted together. Splitting up will remove this icon, or you can switch to your partner and change the identifying information the police have on them, such as their outfit.

CCTV – There are two icons for this one. The Camera means CCTV footage is stored locally somewhere and can be destroyed. The Cloud icon means the footage is stored in the cloud and is untouchable, so all you can do is get out of there. Bank Jobs are one of the most common places you can expect to see the Cloud icon.

This CCTV logo next to “Destroy Footage” denotes the Heat icon that will be cleared.

Clearing all these icons is important to avoid gaining police attention, whether they've spotted you already or not. If you’re spotted by cops after you’ve only cleared a few recognition icons, you’ll likely have to clear basic recognition markers like appearance and outfit all over again.

Now that we've touched on Heat, let's get to what all the different star colors and levels mean.

Unless you commit a crime directly in front of a cop, a cop is the victim, or it's a large scale crime immediately reported by a dispatcher (like stealing a plane), you'll receive gray stars when a crime is first reported. Gray stars mean the cops have been called, and they're on their way to the scene with your description. They haven't seen you yet, but you can easily tell what they know about you based on the heat icons that appear below your initial Wanted level . You can earn more than one gray star over time, but it requires more bystanders to report further crimes. This is the best time to flee the scene, when the stars are still gray. Since the cops haven't gained a visual on your person, there's still a ton you can do to throw the cops off your trail. As soon as cops get eyes on you, those gray stars turn into white stars and a full pursuit starts. It's much easier to gain stars, and much more difficult to escape without escalating the situation.

You’ll also see the Wanted stars turn gray if the cops lose sight of you after they have your description.

When an incident has been called into the police, but they don't yet know your identity, you'll see unfilled stars with a white outline. In our experience, this most often happens if you clear your heat icons before you're spotted by police, or when gunfire is reported but not seen- if you're shooting up an empty alleyway for example. As long as you don't do anything else to draw attention to yourself, it should be easy to evade detection. Regardless, it's a good idea to leave the area.

Drop the gun, Lucia! We have a limited window to get away with this!

Once cops have eyes on you, the gray stars will turn white, and they're in full pursuit. An important nuance when police first respond is that they'll often use Tasers rather than lethal weapons if you yourself aren't armed with a weapon. Once you pull a gun, they'll respond in kind. The actions you take while cops are in pursuit make a huge difference in escalating star rankings. Simply driving away won't often add more stars to your warning level, but it will be harder to lose the cops. Pulling a gun and giving yourself options can make it easier to lose the cops, but will quickly escalate your star level. And even deciding where to shoot can escalate that level further; aiming for tires and non-lethal areas (the ones that show up as yellow in focus mode) will raise your level much more slowly than firing into the center mass or heads of officers.

Full red stars mean the police know that you committed a crime in the area you are in, and while they’ve lost you for the moment, the nearby police are on high alert. They are looking for someone who matches your current description, shown to you by the various Heat symbols underneath the stars.

Red outlined stars means the police know there was a crime committed in the area you are currently in, but you no-longer match the description of the person who committed that crime, and they won’t immediately recognize you. They are on high-alert in this area though, and they will respond quickly to any crimes committed nearby.

When you only have 1 star , expect a minor police presence usually consisting of one to three squad cars. This initial response is often nonlethal unless you pull a weapon yourself, and cops will use tasers. Tasers rapidly drain your stamina. If it's drained too much from being tased and you get grabbed by an officer, you'll see a small lightning bolt icon next to the button it tells you to mash, and it will be much more difficult to free yourself. Here are examples of reported crimes that elicit 1 star.

Grand theft auto (when no tracker is installed)

When you're still at only 1 star, evading the police is simple (especially if they haven't seen you yet) as you can move out of the initial search radius before they arrive. If you’re spotted because you didn't leave the area quickly enough, as long as you break line of sight and hide, the cops give up the search quickly. Alternatively, if you plan ahead, you can clear your heat icons by either removing your mask, changing your accessories, or changing your outfit from the trunk of your car.

You'll often get to 2 stars by not fleeing a 1 star situation, or by resisting officers who arrive at the scene. There are also a few crimes we've found that will immediately earn you 2 stars when you have none:

Grand theft auto (when car has an advanced tracker that activates)

Putting hands on a cop is an immediate 2 Star Rating.

When you get to two stars, expect an escalation from the cops, in both number and aggression. This can still just mean tasers if you haven't yet pulled a gun, but if you continue to be violent, they may very well pull real firearms while still at this level.

If you’re hiding in a stationery vehicle, you can press Circle / B to duck down and hide.

Killing a cop or multiple civilians earns you 3 stars quickly, but it doesn't even have to be that excessive. Even just beating up about a dozen cops without killing any can still escalate you to this level, or if a car chase goes on long enough. Committing a string of robberies can also quickly escalate you to the 3-star level. When you get to 3 stars, police will begin using longarms (like rifles and shotguns, rather than just pistols), be equipped with body armor, drive bigger vehicles that will ram into yours if you’re on the road,organize roadblocks on nearby streets, and the dispatcher will call in air support to help spot you.

If you decide to flee on foot rather than in a vehicle, the K9 unit may also be dispatched. You can hear when this happens over the police scanner, and you'll continue to hear barking as they get closer.

Helicopters will make it much more difficult to break visual contact with the police, but you do still have an opportunity to get away; if you listen to the cops' chatter, they'll tell you when the chopper has to return to their base to refuel. If you're in a long chase, as soon as the stars turn gray when the chopper leaves, you need to break line of sight (usually by leaving the main roads) and hide. This is your best chance to escape after escalating to this level. You can also fire on choppers a few times to get them to flee.

These are a few crimes that will also immediately earn you a 3 Star Wanted level:

Killing multiple civilians with an explosive

Killing multiple cops or many more civilians will eventually net you 4 stars . This is when dispatchers will call in the SWAT Team, and you’ll begin to be fired on by choppers. If you’re in a car they’ll try to shoot you in addition to attempting to disable your vehicle. Dealing with the choppers will be the priority here as they’re much harder to hide from. Shoot the gunners if you can, or even the rotors to cause the chopper to crash.

If SWAT catches up to you, be aware that they come with military-grade vehicles. Their cars are armored like their bodies, and they’ll come equipped with heavy weapons.

One crime that will immediately launch you up to four stars is stealing an airplane from the airport. In that case, make sure you bring a parachute since they’ll scramble fighter jets to send after you.

Reaching 5 stars is the highest Wanted level escalation you can achieve and still possibly escape from. It takes a concerted effort to gain five stars, like killing a ton of cops or civilians, or blowing up multiple vehicles.

Once you reach this level, cops will be hyper aggressive, send in multiple air units and armored cars after you, set up multiple roadblocks, and will continue to search by air long after you've evaded capture. You won't last long in a non-armored vehicle either, as you'll be taking gunfire constantly, and cops will constantly be trying to shoot out your tires.

Reaching 6 stars is different from the other Wanted levels. There's even a pop up that warns you that nothing will stop the cops from hunting you ; they will continue to pursue until you're dead. The entire map will be your “Wanted” area. There's no way to achieve a 6 star Wanted rating by accident; it requires a violent rampage for an extended amount of time and a high body count.

Short of apocalyptic levels of violence, not much else will get you to 6 stars.

We could give you tips to surviving a 6 star ranking, but it would all just be a stall since death or a reload is inevitable.

The most important thing you can do to escape the cops is to avoid being seen (while the stars are still gray) or break their line of sight (after the stars turn white). Running or driving away in a straight line makes it more likely that they can keep eyes on you. So long as they do, the circle on the map in which the cops are looking for you continues to move with you, and you'll have a harder time escaping. It is possible if your car is fast enough to simply get away from them by laying on the accelerator, but it's much more difficult.

Moving in a straight line down the freeway also means that police will know where to set up barricades. These can often be avoided by going offroad for a moment or even veering into oncoming traffic, but it's an extra hazard you'll have to deal with if you continue to move in a straight line.

Making sharp turns, going down narrow backroads, or even ditching your vehicle and escaping on foot are all effective ways to break line of sight. Once you do, the stars will go back to being gray, meaning the cops lost visual. Once you escape the search radius, the stars will flash for a moment before going away. Alternatively, if you hide for long enough after breaking line of sight while still inside the search radius, the stars will turn red, and you'll need to remain hidden for long enough, clear your heat, or leave the radius to get rid of them.

I once hid at a bar after sending Jason to fence our haul. I called him back and had Lucia and Jason drink and dance until the search was called off and the heat went away. GTA 6 provides plenty of ways to creatively lay low and get away with crime.

You can also call on your partner to make a distraction. If you have partner heat, hold D-pad Right on the d-pad and press Triangle / Y to split up and pull some of the heat off both of you. When they’re in the clear, they’ll text you asking if you want to meet back up.

Whether you're Wasted (killed) or Busted (arrested), the result is the same. You'll lose all your Pocket Cash (the money on your person) and a small amount of money out of your checking account.

Unfortunately, surrendering when cops corner you doesn't garner you any sympathy. You'll still get Busted and lose the same amount of money.

Preparing For a Clean Getaway (Avoiding the Police Checklist)

If you plan ahead, there's a good chance you never even need to deal with the cops in the first place. Before committing a premeditated crime, consider going through a pre-crime checklist.

Take time to scope out your target; what are the entrances and exits? How much security is there? You can also preview the building’s layout in the Map.

Put your mask on before entering an area where you want to commit a crime.

After committing the crime, take care of any CCTV footage that's stored on-site before leaving.

After getting out of sight of any witnesses, take your mask off, and take off or put on some sunglasses or a hat to clear your Appearance Heat.

Keep spare changes of clothing in your trunk, and change to clear your Clothing Heat Icon. It’s helpful to have multiple outfits ready in case you’re spotted and need to change again.

If you currently have the Vehicle Heat Icon, ditch your car after you change your clothes.

If you and your partner were seen together, hold D-pad Right on the d-pad and press Triangle / Y to split up and clear the Partner Heat Icon.

If you follow all these rules, you have a much higher chance of scoring a Clean Getaway . You may have some White Outline Stars, but that means the cops have no idea who did it! As long as you leave the area, you're free!

If you want to learn more about how your Criminal Profile can affect how the police interact with you, visit IGN's official Criminal Profile and Consequences guide page.

articles.title: Afternoon Delight Walkthrough - GTA 6 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: After completing your chosen task with Lucia in Grand Theft Auto VI’s Coffee Break main mission, you’ll receive a call from Vicki about hitting
articles.body:
After completing your chosen task with Lucia in Grand Theft Auto VI ’s Coffee Break main mission, you’ll receive a call from Vicki about hitting Delights a few in-game hours later. Chapter 2’s Afternoon Delight mission features a unique opportunity to make a lot of money and help a friend out, and this official IGN GTA 6 guide walks you through it.

Vicki wants to rob her boss and split the cash. Meet her at Delights.

Click on a link below to jump to that section of this guide:

I’d recommend saving the game before starting this mission.

Drive to Delights to get started. If you go with only one lead, the other will join before the mission begins. It’s Girls’ Night, so Jason is told to leave and walks off while you play as Lucia and walk in.

Watch the short scene between Vicki and Lucia until you’re playing back as Jason, who needs to find out why the show hasn’t started.

As soon as you’re Jason, walk straight along the building, then hop the metal fence on the right. You’ll spot an open door right by the fence that leads backstage. Enter to start a cutscene. Inside, Jason sees Frankie trying to wake a dancer who may as well be dead, while the lead dancer, Mario, complains. They notice Jason standing near the door, and Mario likes what he sees.

Your choice on whether to help Frankie and Mario impacts how the rest of this mission plays out. It won’t impact the rest of the game beyond the regular shifting metrics (Criminal Profiles and Jason and Lucia’s relationship), though.

Rewards between the two options Tap to Reveal Still, I’d recommend helping them for a more unique experience. If you end up not liking your choice, you can reload your save, or from the pause menu, choose to reload the last checkpoint or restart the mission.

Click or tap the option you picked to skip directly to the walkthrough for each of the mission variants:

Jason’s rejection quickly leads to Mario and his backup dancer leaving. Frankie scrambles for a show replacement. As Lucia, wait until Frankie’s underwhelming show gets going. This takes about two minutes. Not long into it, the bottom right corner of the screen pulses with Jason’s profile, indicating it’s time to swap. Press and hold D-pad Right on the D-Pad and tap R1 / RB to shift to his perspective. Jason walks on stage, and he’s armed. The dull party at Delights turns into a shootout. The bikers, members of the Final Chapter, will likely be the first to fire. There’s one to the right of the stage, just behind the bride-to-be. There should be another man around the corner near the pool table. After he’s down, keep walking back toward the front and the bar to get to the office. You can stop to rob the women, too, if you want.

When you get to the bar, you’ll come across one more biker taking cover behind the counter. With him down, you can walk through the door by the bar to get to Frankie’s office. Pick up the three stacks of bill across Frankie’s desk and the side table behind the desk, then hit the safe. Frankie’s safe code is Tap to Reveal , the number Vicki texted earlier. Inside the safe are two stacks of marked bills. Collect them. As you do, you’ll earn an extra $1,800. Notice that you’ll also have video camera heat. You won’t find the security footage in the office this time, so ignore it and leave. You can take the money from the register at the bar, too, if you want, but keep an eye on the front door hallway as you do it.

Move out with Lucia when you’re ready, and if you haven’t encountered them already, you’ll run into two more armed members of the Final Chapter in the front door hallway. Get rid of them, then run outside. If you take too long in Delights, a group of bikers may be waiting for you. Otherwise, they’ll start rolling up one-by-one. Get in your car quickly.

Good choice. Mario goes on stage, riling up the women while Lucia watches. You’re briefly able to look around as Jason in the wings until he’s told to get out on stage. There, dance for the crowd and follow the prompts to put on a good show. After some time dancing, Mario goes down to give lap dances and generally dance closer to the women. You can follow slowly after, but don’t forget to dance and add extra flourishes with Square / X .

To move the mission along, walk up to Mario, who is maybe too enthusiastically giving a lap dance to Lucia. Press Triangle / Y to move Mario out of the way. Instead, you swap perspectives to Lucia. As Lucia, you can let the lap dance from Mario play out. If you back out of it relatively quickly, you’ll earn relationship points for Jason and Lucia and Jason takes over. One short lap dance later, Jason is called back to the stage for more dancing and Vicki calls Lucia over. There’s enough going on to make for a clean robbery. Walk through the kitchen back to the office. There’s some coffee on the counter if you want a quick Stamina and Focus boost.

Once you’re in the office, grab the money from the desk and another bundle from the side table behind the desk. There’s nothing else to collect here, so move on to the safe. Enter the code Vicki sent: Tap to Reveal . Inside, you’ll find two sets of marked bills to collect. Lucia cleans out the safe and two biker guards suddenly walk in, ready to sound the alarm.

Back on the stage, money is flying as Jason and the strippers finish the song. Vicki rushes up to the stage and calls for Jason to help Lucia. As you walk back toward the bar, Jason will grab a pool cue from the table and break it over his knee. Approach the door leading to the manager’s office by the bar and a Final Chapter biker steps in the way. Don’t give him a chance to throw a punch. One hit with the pool cue knocks him right out. As soon as you walk through the door, Jason is attacked by another biker. This scene is scripted, so you can’t punch out the guy properly until Lucia finishes off the two guys in the office, but keep pressing Square / X to keep punching him anyway. As Lucia runs out the door, you can knock out the biker. Follow her through and be sure to loot the guys you knocked out quickly to get a few extra dollars.

From here, you can stay and fight the Final Chapter members challenging Jason to the delight of onlookers, or you can rush past the few in the entry area and follow Lucia. If you stay in the strip club too long, though, Final Chapter bikers from the other end of the building may start shooting. It’s not worth hanging around to deal with them, so run out to meet Lucia. You’ll get one of two scenes of running to the car depending on how fast you left Delights. Now all that’s left to do is escape the Final Chapter bikers.

Playing as Lucia, you’ll need to escape the Final Chapter bikers by any means necessary. Jason will shoot at them, but you should provide either extra fire or hit the motorcycles with the car to knock out pursuers. If you stay on the main road in Port Gellhorn too long, the police get called in, adding an extra layer to the chase. As always, the best way to get away when you’re being followed is by making sudden turns, breaking line of sight, and if needed, hiding somewhere offroad. This part of the mission ends once you’re in the clear of both Final Chapter and cops. Next, you’ll need to meet Vicki.

If you helped Mario, you’ll need to either return to the motel or the thrift store after you’ve gotten away from the bikers, whichever is nearer. You’ll swap to Jason automatically and must get clothes before you can close out the mission. Get back in the car and the two receive the meetup spot for Vicki.

Vicki waits for Lucia and Jason at the back of an overgrown bumper cars ride, looking out at the water. Approach her to enter the final cutscene of the mission.

Vicki walks off with the bag, leaving Jason and Lucia to the rest of their day. The two continue to talk and Jason texts his friend Dre’Quan to get an update on the potential place to stay in Vice City, leading to an end to the mission.

Before leaving the amusement park, scan the Ferris wheel with the WAiNK It app to log it to your collection.

If you haven’t reached the $15,000 needed to save for the move to Vice City, the next best way to speed that up is by selling a few stolen cars to Moses .

After you’ve reached the required amount, you’ll get a text from Cal a few hours later that kicks off the next mission, Checking Out .

This walkthrough features some first-person elements. Those come from IGN's GTA 6 Lead Editor, Miranda Sanchez. You can learn more about them and their experience on the About the Guide Editors page.

articles.title: Checking Out Walkthrough - GTA 6 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: In the final mission of Grand Theft Auto VI’s Chapter 2, it’s finally time for Jason and Lucia to call it on Port Gellhorn and move to bigger
articles.body:
In the final mission of Grand Theft Auto VI ’s Chapter 2, it’s finally time for Jason and Lucia to call it on Port Gellhorn and move to bigger things in Vice City. This official IGN GTA 6 guide walks you through the Checking Out main mission.

When ready, pack up and leave the motel to meet Dre’Quan in Vice City.

Click on a link below to jump to that section of this guide:

To unlock the final main mission in Port Gellhorn, you’ll need to complete the the Afternoon Delight main mission . Additionally, while not necessary, having $15,000 in your BuckMe checking account unlocks the mission faster.

After those two are complete and a few in-game hours later, Cal texts Jason and Lucia an article about a murdered couple found near Port Gellhorn, worrying it’s them. Well, they’re not dead and can read the text. They decide the men looking for them are way too close and it’s time to move on.

Be sure to buff Jason and Lucia’s stats. An apple and bottle of water from the kitchen can get all their stats buffed quickly.

Have you been calling Jason and Lucia’s friends? If not, give Cal a call for a quick extra interaction. It doesn’t hurt to check in with their friends after major events.

When you’re ready, start this mission by opening the bathroom door to check on the case. Jason and Lucia pack. They’re interrupted by an aggressive knock from Linda, who they brush off as fast as they can before they depart. As Jason finishes up in the motel room, he hears yelling out front. Trouble has finally arrived.

Grab the Moreland 850 Shotgun from the bed. As you approach the door, a man kicks it in. Shoot him immediately with the shotgun, then immediately get to cover once you step outside. There’ll be at least three or four men targeting the door from the street and their own cover. The shotgun has surprisingly good range, and a lot of ammo. You can steal one of the strangers’ rifles but be careful moving out of cover when the fight is still early. After you eliminate the four or five guys in front of the apartment, move toward the kitchen to meet up with Lucia.

You can leave Lucia and escape alone, but you’ll take a hit to their relationship if you do. As you move up the street more guys arrive, also equipped with SMGs and rifles.

If you haven’t explored much as Jason since he recovered, play carefully as he may not have much – or any – Zombix or Adrenaline on him. There’s some in the kitchen, but you’re better off clearing the street before running in to meet Lucia.

You’ll have to eliminate about seven or eight men from the parking lot. You’ll know the area is clear when you get the cinematic kill shot on the last guy standing. You’ll get a short scene of Lucia choking a guy in the kitchen either when you meet her in the kitchen or when you clear out the motel parking lot. After it, you’ll switch to Lucia.

From here, you can swap between Jason and Lucia as they hold up in the motel kitchen. At least six more men arrive from the north side of the motel, peppering the kitchen with gunfire. If you happened to pick up any Frag Grenades during your journey in Port Gellhorn, now is a great time to use them or any other cool gear.

Low on health? Grab a Zombix and an Adrenaline from the first aid cabinet hanging between the coffee machine and the sink.

Two more men approach from the street on the east side of the kitchen. They’re not smart enough to hide behind cover, though, so taking them out from the kitchen window should be quick. While you do this, the cops should start showing up too.

The road is clear and Jason tells Lucia to follow him out. He grabs a car from the street, but a gunman on a motorcycle and the cops separate them. Be sure to shoot the gunman dead fast or else you’ll have to restart at the checkpoint. Lucia hops on the dirtbike while Jason drives away from the cops. Follow Jason through to the construction site and shoot at the tires of the cop cars as you have them in your sights. Lucia is vulnerable to gunfire on the bike, making this a great time to use Adrenaline if you have one available. If you get too far behind Jason or lose sight of the car, don’t forget to use Focus to find his driving path. You can also see his pink marker on the map.

As you get into town, more gunmen in cars join the chase. Follow Jason through the neighborhood streets. He’ll turn onto the large road that runs along the train tracks after that. The mostly straight road gives you a chance to catch up, making your new goal to get close and jump into the car. Shoot out the tires – or drivers – of any who get in your way. Like with other moving jumps, stay close to Jason’s car while maintaining speed and hold Square / X to make it across successfully.

Jason hands Lucia a rifle once she’s settled in the car. Similar to the end of Chapter 1, the only way to escape now is by shooting out the tires, engine, or driver of any car that gets too close. The final pursuing police car manages to crash into a truck that spins out and blocks the road, making a clear escape for Jason and Lucia.

The mission ends with the scene of the two escaping and leads right into the next mission, Welcome to Vice City .

articles.title: Pick Up a Gun Walkthrough - GTA 6 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Chapter 2 in GTA 6 begins with a bunch of activities for Lucia to take on while she waits for Jason to heal. Because Jason and Lucia lost everything at the end
articles.body:
Chapter 2 in GTA 6 begins with a bunch of activities for Lucia to take on while she waits for Jason to heal. Because Jason and Lucia lost everything at the end of Chapter 1, Chapter 2 begins with them rebuilding their money, arsenal, vehicles, and even wardrobe. One of the first early optional missions is to Pick Up a Gun.

Using the map, you can see that the gun shop for this area is called Gellhorn Outfitters, and it's found along the beach on the western side of Port Gellhorn. The location for the store will be marked on your map, so head over to it when you can.

Once you enter Gellhorn Outfitters, an on-screen will tell you to buy a gun or recover one from the locker.

Recovering from the locker is the much cheaper choice, as it will house any weapons you might've stored in the gun locker or in your personal vehicle during chapter 1. Once you grab your guns from the locker, the mission will disappear.

At this point in the story, you will not have much money. Depending on what order you are doing the beginning missions, you'll likely have anywhere from a couple hundred dollars to maybe five or six hundred. This doesn't leave you a ton of options when it comes to buying a gun, but there are some.

Under the pistols section, there is a Scorpio Nipper .38 for only $495. To complete this mission, this is likely your best bet, as anything better will cost you upwards of $1000.

Once you have your guns, simply leave the shop and the mission will be cleared from your list or optional missions. There is no reward for completing this mission.

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto VI launches to rave reviews after 13-year wait
articles.summary: Critics hail GTA 6 as a ‘masterpiece’, ‘spectacular’, and an ‘astonishing American epic’.
articles.body:
Grand Theft Auto VI has launched to rave reviews, in one of the most hotly anticipated releases in gaming history.

Gamers got their hands on the latest instalment of the GTA franchise on Thursday, as critics hailed the open-world game as a “masterpiece”, “spectacular”, and an “astonishing American epic”.

The immersive game had an aggregate score of 99 out of 100 on Metacritic, based on more than 150 reviews, as it began dropping on game consoles worldwide from midnight.

“Exquisitely detailed, endlessly ripe for experimentation, and uncompromisingly engineered, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played,” critic Luke Reilly wrote in a gushing review for gaming website IGN.

“Accepting that GTA 6 is very much not real also makes it all the more astonishing how much the game is very real,” reviewer Jordan Minor wrote in PCMag.

Grand Theft Auto VI follows the exploits of Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, a Bonnie and Clyde-like duo who become entangled in a criminal conspiracy after a seemingly easy score goes awry.

Players have free rein to explore the hyper-realistic fictional state of Leonida and its coastal metropolis of Vice City, stand-ins for Florida and Miami.

Like previous entries in the series, Grand Theft Auto VI features graphic depictions of crime and violence, with players able to mow down pedestrians in stolen vehicles and engage in shootouts with police.

The game, developed by New York-based Rockstar Games at an estimated cost of more than $1bn, is the first instalment in the series since the release of Grand Theft Auto V in 2013.

Originally set to go on sale in 2025, the release was delayed twice to allow developers to polish up gameplay.

Grand Theft Auto VI, which is available on the PlayStation 5 and the Xbox Series, is likely to be the most lucrative release in the history of the gaming industry, which is projected to be worth as much as $350bn by the end of the decade.

Pre-orders for Grand Theft Auto VI exceeded an estimated 15.8 million units as of November 17, generating $1.54bn in revenue, according to the market intelligence platform Sensor Tower.

The GTA series began in 1997 with the launch of Grand Theft Auto, a 2D top-down open-world game available on the personal computer, PlayStation and Game Boy Color.

images.caption: A billboard announcing the release of the Grand Theft Auto VI video game is displayed near Times Square, on November 17, 2026, in New York, US [Yuki Iwamura/AP Photo]
